# Jev was judging against a ticket that no longer existed

Three clarify attempts scored 0.75, to two decimal places, each time. Identical scores across
substantive edits are not a judgement, they are a signal that the input is not what it appears to be.

Asking the same record with a short ticket text scored 0.86. The state the harness sends carries
`ticket_text` from record 1's snapshot, frozen at `harness start`. SEEN-094's snapshot still demanded
gitleaks and `pnpm audit`, which moved to SEEN-090 earlier today, so the model was correctly reporting
that the record did not resolve everything the ticket asked. It was reading a ticket that no longer
exists.

Tickets are amended during clarify in this project, routinely and deliberately: SEEN-087's two
criteria, SEEN-006's AC4, SEEN-089's AC3 and SEEN-094's own template criterion. Judging a record
against the document it was written before is how a resolved question keeps reading as an open one,
and it would have got worse with every ticket.

Fixed here with a test: the gates read the ticket file as it stands, and fall back to the snapshot
only when the file is gone. The snapshot stays in the journal, where it is evidence of what the work
was originally asked to do, which is a different question from what it is being judged against.

This is the third harness defect surfaced by working a product ticket, after the override that did
not exist and the coverage baseline breaking ADR 0002. All three were found by using the thing rather
than by reading it.
